name: Make a private fund commitment
summary: A private markets team (private equity, real estate, infrastructure or private credit) takes a general partner's fund offering from first screen through due diligence, committee approval and negotiation of the partnership agreement and side letter. The work covers data room review, track record analysis, meetings with the general partner, references, operational due diligence, fee and term analysis, a pacing check that splits the commitment across client accounts, the memo, an independent risk opinion and the committee decision. Elapsed time is driven by meeting slots, committee dates and rounds of comments with the general partner's counsel, all against the fund's closing deadline.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion whose private market teams made roughly ten fund commitments a year, mostly held in segregated client accounts.
baseline.notes: In 2021 private equity made four fund commitments totalling $1.5 billion; in 2020 three buyout commitments totalling $1 billion plus real estate and credit funds.

trigger: A general partner or placement agent sends a fund offering that the team logs and screens against the annual pacing plan.
end_state: The committee-approved commitment has agreed partnership agreement and side letter terms and a client account split, and is handed to the closing team; or the offering is declined or rejected.

volume.seasonality: Follows general partners' fundraising cycles; year-end and first-quarter closes are common.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file. Releases name about 8 fund commitments in 2020 and 6 in 2021, near the low end of the range; cases are counted when they reach the pipeline decision, and about 25% are declined or rejected.

Deal lead for private equity commitments, about 45% of commitments (mgr2021: four PE fund commitments in 2021). Loaded cost from the organisation file, which prices investment professionals from estimated total pay; the Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto median of $41.60 an hour is base pay only.
Data room, track record and reference work on private equity commitments.
Pipeline decision, memo review.

steps.name: Log offering and do first screen
steps.description: A general partner or placement agent sends a fund offering (pitch book and private placement memorandum). The principal logs it in the team's pipeline tracker, reads the materials and checks fit with the annual pacing plan, strategy, the relationship (re-up or new manager) and prior fund performance, then writes a one-page screening note.

control.basis: Annual investment plan: commitments only within the approved pacing and strategy plan

evidence.note: nc_imd: annual work plan sets commitment pace, opportunities logged in a database and screened on plan fit, history with the firm, prior fund performance and terms. Times tier C.

steps.name: Decide to start due diligence
steps.description: At the weekly team pipeline meeting the managing director reviews the screening note against competing offerings and the team's capacity and decides whether to commit due diligence resources.

evidence.note: nc_imd: directors choose where due diligence resources will be deployed at regular staff meetings. Decline share counts only offerings that reached this meeting; tier C.

steps.name: Review confidentiality agreement
steps.description: Investment counsel reviews the general partner's confidentiality agreement and data room terms, adding the public-sector records and regulator disclosure carve-outs the organisation needs, and returns it for signature.

control.basis: Legal sign-off required on confidentiality agreements; public records carve-out

evidence.note: cooley_sl lists confidentiality and public-records carve-outs among institutional LP requests. Times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for data room and questionnaire
steps.description: The general partner opens the virtual data room and supplies its completed due diligence questionnaire, draft partnership agreement, track record data and predecessor fund reports.

evidence.note: The ILPA DDQ appendix lists the documents a GP's diligence package should hold. Times tier C.

steps.name: Review data room and questionnaire
steps.description: The associate works through the data room: private placement memorandum, draft partnership agreement, questionnaire answers, audited reports of predecessor funds and advisory committee minutes, and builds the due diligence checklist and question list for the general partner.

evidence.note: ILPA DDQ 2.0 topics and requested documents; nc_imd lists PPM review. Times tier C.

steps.name: Analyse track record
steps.description: The associate rebuilds deal-level cash flows from the track record file, calculates net and gross IRR, multiples, realised and unrealised splits, loss ratios and dispersion, compares them with public market equivalents and peer benchmarks, and attributes returns by deal partner.

error.defect_description: Unrealised values taken at face value, overstating performance.

evidence.note: Quantitative analysis of performance and comparison with competing offerings (nc_imd); ILPA DDQ track record section. Times tier C.

steps.name: Meet general partner team
steps.description: The principal and associate hold management meetings with the fund's partners, often at the general partner's office, covering strategy, deal sourcing, value creation, team stability, succession and the questions from the data room review. Some offerings are dropped here.

evidence.note: Manager presentations and onsite visits are part of intensive due diligence (nc_imd). Times and drop rate tier C.

steps.name: Call references
steps.description: The associate calls references given by the general partner and others found independently: other limited partners, portfolio company chief executives, co-investors and former employees.

evidence.note: Reference checks with other investors, limited partners and consultants (nc_imd). Times tier C.

steps.name: Conduct operational due diligence on the general partner
steps.description: The manager research analyst reviews the operations, accounting and valuation, reporting, compliance and data security sections of the questionnaire, the fund administrator arrangement, cash movement controls and valuation policy, and holds a call with the general partner's chief financial officer.

evidence.note: sbai2024: for private equity and real estate ODD is often embedded in the investment team's due diligence; ILPA DDQ sections 13, 15 and 18; aima_journal on GPs asking for reviews at short notice. Times tier C.

steps.name: Sign off operational assessment
steps.description: The head of manager research approves the operational rating, notes conditions to be secured in the side letter, or asks the general partner to fix a weakness before the team proceeds.

control.basis: Operational due diligence policy: an acceptable rating is required before a commitment is recommended

next.condition: general partner asked to remediate or clarify

evidence.note: ODD veto rights and their rare use (sbai2024). Rates tier C.

steps.name: Wait for general partner's remediation
steps.description: The general partner provides documents, policy changes or a commitment to appoint an independent administrator or change controls; the analyst then reassesses.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Analyse fees and terms
steps.description: The principal models management fees, carried interest, hurdle, fee offsets and expenses, compares the draft partnership agreement with the ILPA Principles and the organisation's preferred terms (key person, removal, advisory committee, reporting) and drafts the list of changes and side letter requests.

evidence.note: ILPA Principles 3.0 on fees, governance and side letters; nc_imd on preferred terms; cooley_sl on typical side letter requests. Times tier C.

steps.name: Run conflict, sanctions and placement agent checks
steps.description: The compliance analyst screens the general partner, its principals and any placement agent against sanctions and adverse media, collects placement agent disclosures and staff conflict declarations, and confirms clearance.

control.basis: Code of conduct, conflict of interest and placement agent disclosure rules (independent compliance review as in nc_imd)

evidence.note: nc_imd requires placement agent disclosure forms, conflict certifications and an independent compliance review. Times tier C.

steps.name: Size and split commitment across client accounts
steps.description: The total portfolio manager runs the commitment pacing model for each client portfolio, checking its private market target weight, existing unfunded commitments and liquidity, and proposes how the commitment is split across the client accounts (or pool) that will hold it.

error.defect_description: Unfunded commitments understated, overcommitting a smaller client.

evidence.note: The organisation file says most private assets were in segregated client accounts in the period, so each commitment is split among clients; method and times tier C.

steps.name: Draft investment memo
steps.description: The principal, with the associate, writes the investment committee memo: strategy and market, team, track record, strengths and weaknesses, due diligence and operational findings, fees and terms, sizing and split across client accounts, and risks with mitigants.

error.defect_description: Weak competitive comparison or unsupported return expectations.

evidence.note: nc_imd: recommendation memo with SWOT, background, returns, merits and risks, competitive analysis, operational assessment and expected terms. Times tier C.

steps.name: Review memo
steps.description: The managing director challenges the memo's case, sizing and terms and returns comments; most memos get one round of edits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Obtain independent risk opinion
steps.description: The investment risk manager reviews concentration by manager, vintage and sector, leverage, currency, liquidity and fit with each client's risk budget, and writes the risk opinion for the committee paper.

control.basis: Investment risk policy: independent risk opinion required for every commitment paper (see new-investment-risk-review)

evidence.note: Described in the organisation file's new-investment-risk-review process; times tier C.

steps.name: Submit paper to investment committee
steps.description: The investment office checks the paper against the template, places it on the next committee agenda and circulates the pack; papers wait for the next meeting unless a closing deadline forces a special one.

evidence.note: Committee cadence assumed every two to three weeks.

steps.name: Investment committee decides
steps.description: The investment committee chaired by the CIO hears the deal team and approves, approves with conditions, defers or rejects. Commitments above the committee's delegated limit go to the board.

control.basis: Investment committee terms of reference and board-approved delegated authority limits

evidence.note: Conditional approval before negotiation (nc_imd); the organisation file sends deals above the CEO's authority to the board. Shares tier C.

steps.name: Board approves large commitment
steps.description: For commitments above the delegated limit, the paper goes to the next board or investment committee of the board, which approves or rejects it.

evidence.note: Board meets about quarterly; share of commitments needing board approval is an assumption.

steps.name: Send legal instruction
steps.description: The principal instructs investment counsel with the approved commitment amount by client account, committee conditions, the requested partnership agreement changes and side letter requests, and the general partner's closing date.

evidence.note: Negotiation follows approval (nc_imd). Times tier C.

steps.name: Mark up partnership agreement and draft side letter
steps.description: Investment counsel, using outside counsel on large or complex funds, marks up the partnership agreement and drafts the side letter covering tax, reporting, confidentiality, sovereign immunity, most favoured nation rights and the committee's conditions, and sends them to the general partner's counsel.

evidence.note: cooley_sl lists 21 side letter provision categories; ILPA notes side letter costs can be sizeable. Times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for general partner's counsel
steps.description: The general partner's counsel consolidates comments from many limited partners and replies with positions on the partnership agreement comments and the side letter.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of turnaround during a fundraise.

steps.name: Review responses and negotiate
steps.description: Counsel reviews the general partner's response, confers with the principal on business points such as fees and key person terms, decides what to concede and sends a revised draft. Two or three rounds are common.

evidence.note: Number of rounds is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve final negotiated terms
steps.description: The principal, with the managing director, confirms that the final partnership agreement and side letter meet the committee's conditions and that the client account split is unchanged.

control.basis: Committee conditions must be met before closing; deal team confirms in writing

evidence.note: nc_imd: external counsel memo comparing final terms with preferred terms before final approval. Times tier C.

steps.name: Hand off to closing
steps.description: Counsel sends the execution versions, side letter, committee approval and client account split to the closing team, which prepares subscription documents, anti-money-laundering forms and tax forms, and records key terms such as fees and most favoured nation rights in the term tracker.

evidence.note: Boundary with private-deal-closing-funding as set out in the organisation file.

exceptions.name: Operational weakness at the general partner
exceptions.description: ODD finds a weakness (self-administration, weak cash controls, valuation policy) and the general partner is asked to remediate or accept side letter protections.

exceptions.name: Commitment above committee limit
exceptions.description: The commitment exceeds delegated authority and waits for the board.

exceptions.name: Extra negotiation rounds
exceptions.description: The general partner's counsel rejects key side letter or partnership agreement points and further rounds are needed, sometimes pushing the commitment to a later closing.

exceptions.name: Most favoured nation election after final close
exceptions.description: After the fund's final close the general partner sends an MFN disclosure package and counsel has about 30 days to elect provisions; this falls after the case ends and is handled in investment-legal-agreements.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from logging the offering to terms agreed and handed to closing
benchmarks.population: Fund commitments by Canadian public asset owners (author's estimate)

evidence.note: Fundraising windows of about 12 months after first close (ilpa_p3) bound the process; a quarter of investors take more than 12 months to make a commitment counting relationship building (pfcfo2014). Re-ups with known managers run faster than new relationships.

pain_points.description: General partners set closing deadlines that squeeze due diligence, risk review and committee dates; ODD reviews are sometimes requested at a week's notice.

evidence.note: aima_journal panellists called a week's notice impractical.

pain_points.description: Track record data arrives in many formats and is rebuilt by hand in spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Typical of the period.

pain_points.description: Customised questionnaires and repeated document requests burden both sides; the ILPA DDQ exists to cut this.
Side letter negotiation runs in rounds through the general partner's counsel, who batches comments from many limited partners.

sources.title: External Investment Manager and Vehicle Selection Policy and Procedures (IMD-POL-1001)
sources.publisher: North Carolina Department of State Treasurer, Investment Management Division
sources.supports: Public pension manager and fund selection steps: director proposes search rationale, staff and consultant roles and criteria for CIO approval; first-level database screen and short-form questionnaire; requests for information to typically 3 or more managers; screen of responses; preliminary conference calls covering operations, risk, compliance, conflicts and willingness to accept preferred terms, with informal reference calls; finalist interviews with CIO, risk, operations and compliance invited. For private funds: annual work plan sets commitment pace; opportunity database; preliminary fund screen; intensive due diligence (PPM review, performance and fee analysis, comparison with competing offerings, presentations or onsite visits, reference checks, risk and operational review, conflicts, placement agent forms, willingness to accept preferred terms); limited partnership offering periods cycle every 4 to 6 years; investment recommendation memo with SWOT; documents requested (code of ethics, compliance manual, valuation policy, SSAE 16 report, insurance, ADV, audited financials); independent compliance review; conditional approval before negotiation; external counsel negotiates and writes a memo comparing terms with preferred terms; final approval and execution; no-contact communication protocol.

sources.title: ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0
sources.supports: Standard LP due diligence questionnaire in 20 sections (firm, fund, succession and key persons, strategy, co-investments, GP-led secondaries, credit facilities, investment process, team, alignment, market, fund terms, governance, risk and compliance, track record, accounting and valuation, reporting, legal, data security and third parties, ESG, diversity) with a requested-documents appendix (LPA, PPM, predecessor fund reports, audited financials, examples of capital call and distribution notices); asks whether LPs get more than 10 business days' notice of capital calls and asks the GP to describe its procedures for capital movements.

sources.title: ILPA DDQ 2.0 User Guide (version 1.0)
sources.supports: Released 9 November 2021; aims to cut the burden of redundant customised DDQs; built around private equity and only a starting point for real estate, credit and infrastructure; GPs may answer sensitive questions in person.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0
sources.supports: Capital calls should follow the ILPA standardised format with fee and carry detail and the LP's percentage, with quarterly projections of calls; LPs should have a window of at least 10 business days to respond to capital call requests; ILPA Capital Call and Distribution Notice Template dated 2011; side letter negotiation costs can be sizeable and GPs should disclose side letters; fundraising should end within a reasonable period after initial close, for example 12 months.

sources.title: Primer: Side Letters in Private Equity and Venture Capital Funds
sources.supports: Institutional LP side letter requests (reporting, tax, confidentiality and public-records carve-outs, advisory committee seats, sanctions and placement agent representations, transfers, sovereign immunity); 21 provision categories; MFN eligibility tiered by commitment size; at the end of fundraising the GP sends an MFN disclosure package and investors often have 30 days to elect.

sources.title: The model manager posts solid 2020 return, meets benchmark index (news release)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: External manager roster cut from 200 to 124 in 2020, fund-of-funds eliminated, new strategic partnerships; $10 million of investment management fees saved; 2020 private commitments: three mid-market buyout fund commitments totalling $1 billion, real estate funds (KingSett Affordable Housing, Breakthrough Life Science, Dermody Industrial III), credit funds (Sagard Credit Partners II, Oaktree Opportunities XI).

sources.title: The model manager posts 2021 net return of 9.6%, outperforms benchmark (news release)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: Private equity made four new fund commitments totalling $1.5 billion with new managers Ardian, GI Partners, KKR and Peloton in 2021; US$500 million commitment with new credit strategic partner Ares; initial investor in Brookfield Global Transition Fund; 35 direct and co-investment transactions; AUM $79 billion.

sources.title: LP due diligence crossing year marks
sources.supports: A quarter of investors take more than 12 months to make a single fund commitment.

sources.title: SBAI 2024 Operational Due Diligence Practices Survey
sources.supports: 70% of responding institutional investors have dedicated ODD teams, 80% of which report outside the investment function; 77% do a full ODD review at the start of a new manager relationship; 60% conduct onsite reviews for new managers and 7% do not; results go to the investment committee alone for 50%; 32% of ODD teams have a formal veto, used rarely or at most once a year by 73% of those; only 7% monitor managers less than annually, with a trend to risk-based monitoring; 59% use bespoke DDQs; 41% say they do not always have enough time to complete an ODD review; for private markets ODD is often embedded in the investment team's due diligence.

sources.title: Operational due diligence: what are investors seeking? (AIMA Journal, edition 120)
sources.supports: ODD teams collect documents before meetings, focus meeting time on the highest-risk areas and review policies, compliance controls and legal documents; ODD meetings now run at least twice as long as the couple of hours they once took; private market managers sometimes ask for a review on a week's notice, which panellists called impractical.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst near Toronto (ON), NOC 11101
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $27.97, median $41.60, high $73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: Steps show a private equity commitment (md_private_equity, principal_private_equity, associate_private_equity). Real estate, infrastructure and private credit commitments follow the same steps with their own managing director, principal and associate or analyst, and FTE is split by an assumed share of commitments (45/20/15/20).

associate_private_equity and the other teams' associates and analysts are not in the process map roles but do most of the data room, track record and reference work; head_manager_research, compliance_analyst, investment_risk_manager, investment_office_manager, cio and investment_counsel appear for steps that link to other processes.

The case ends when terms are agreed and handed to closing. Subscription documents, anti-money-laundering and tax forms, signatures, acceptance by the general partner and set-up in the private markets system belong to private-deal-closing-funding, which produces the commitment record, as the organisation file sets out.

Cases are counted when an offering reaches the pipeline decision; about 12% are declined there and 8% later in due diligence (20% declined in all) and 5% are rejected by committee or board, so roughly 1 commitment a month results from 1.3 cases.
8% of commitments are assumed to exceed the committee's delegated limit and need board approval; the threshold is not public.

Volume in the organisation file (about 15 a year) is above the 6 to 8 fund commitments a year named in the 2020 and 2021 releases; unpublished credit, real estate and infrastructure commitments may explain part of the gap.
Hands-on time of roughly 170 to 200 hours per commitment across the team is the author's estimate.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.
